items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: And we had Jake Hanna on drums... in that band

ctx.x: Was that the band that did the European thing?

Yeah but that was after the European tour. Quincy lost a bundle on that tour and was absolutely adamant that he was never going to have a big band again and do that. Because he said he was never going to lose that money again. But that was fun. But then “The Merv Griffin Show” came around in the mid-60s. And we had a pretty good band, Danny Stiles, the late Danny Stiles and myself and Bill Berry and Richie Kamuca, Roger Cumberton and Dick Hafer and Shelly Gold or Shelly Russell, whatever he chose to be called at…
Oh yeah, I remember that name now. Mort Lindsey.

items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: In New York we had Billy Watrous... Trombones, Watrous and Brookmeyer.

ctx.x: And you had to play behind them.

Oh yeah, and, “No that’s too—” and, “well don’t try to fix it up fellas” the trumpet player says “just play it as bad as they want it. I told you it wasn’t going to be fun.” And this is awful. Then Benny Goodman would come on and it would be fine. Count Basie’d come on, it was a great show. Bill Watrous got him to come on, the trombone player.
Who was in the pit, in the show band?
